observation.visible_scene: Close-up of a single cigarette held upright, its lit/ash-capped tip at the top of the white shaft, set against a dark, heavily blurred background containing fixed bokeh light spots (a bright pale-blue circle at left, two gray circles near the top, a large white blur at right).
visible_changes: A smoke column rises from the burning tip and continuously changes shape and direction: near-vertical in frames 1-2, drifting right in frame 3, billowing up-and-left as a darker plume in frame 4, a thin diagonal streak to the upper-left in frame 5, widening again in frames 6-7, and meandering (vertical, diagonal, faint) through frames 8-18.
The visible plume thins and fades around frames 19-20 and is absent from the tip for the remainder of the clip (frames 20-41), leaving only the burning tip with no rising column.

The background bokeh spots stay in the same positions throughout, indicating a stationary camera; a small warm/orange bokeh spot appears and shifts on the right side during the early-mid frames (e.g. frames 3, 8, 9), consistent with a background light rather than the cigarette.
The white shaft of the cigarette remains at the same position and roughly the same length; only the small ash/ember cap at the tip shows minor shape variation frame to frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the smoke column reappears after the excerpt ends, or what caused it to stop being visible (a draft, a disturbance to the ember, or simply thinning below the visibility threshold).
Any change in the cigarette's length or the ember's brightness before the crop begins or after it ends.
uncertain_details: The exact amount of ash/ember consumption at the tip is hard to judge at this resolution.
The disappearance of the plume may be true cessation of visible smoke or merely the column becoming too faint to see.
The nature of the shifting warm bokeh spot on the right is unknown (likely an out-of-focus background light).
